notImplementedOnPlatform.windows: sessions compile but the platform session/TUN path is T6; no Windows run has been recorded

platform.note: Every runtime result here comes from macOS arm64, including the UDP and private-CA cases. A platform difference must be reproduced against the same-platform Mihomo; nothing is claimed for a platform that was not run. The Android VpnService fd data plane (feature `android-vpn`) is exercised on macOS arm64 through a packet-preserving UnixDatagram descriptor; the Android target build (NDK absent in this environment) and real-device traffic remain unverified — see tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t26-android-tunnel.json.

statusVocabulary.implemented: the Rust kernel performs the behaviour and a loopback or pinned-Mihomo test observes it
statusVocabulary.partial: part of the upstream shape works; the missing options are named and rejected explicitly
statusVocabulary.unimplemented: the Rust kernel rejects the entry/field instead of ignoring it

optionPolicy: proxies.rs accepts only the keys its parser read and honoured, plus values Mihomo accepts and ignores: disabled booleans (`udp: false`, `disable-reuse: false`, `packet-addr: false`, `xudp: false`, `v2ray-http-upgrade-fast-open: false`), empty blocks (`grpc-opts: {}`, `ech-opts: {enable: false}`, `smux: {enabled: false}`, `ss-opts: {}`, `shadow-tls-opts: {}`, `restls-opts: {}`, `plugin-opts: {}`) and TLS-only options with TLS off (`skip-cert-verify`, `sni`, `alpn`, `fingerprint`, `certificate`, `private-key`, `name-cert-verify`, `client-fingerprint`, `ech-opts`, `reality-opts`). `reality-opts` and `jls-opts` require fields even when empty (Mihomo's `-t` rejects them), so their empty form fails here too. Every behaviour-changing form that is still a gap fails with the key named; the T27 batch (BasicOption knobs, TLS certificate identities, QUIC congestion/window tuning, socks5 UDP) is implemented and no longer listed as `notImplemented`. tool/kernel-compat/option-probe.mjs compares the no-op and enabled forms against the pinned Mihomo `-t` and writes evidence/option-matrix.txt. A `udp: true` proxy with `dialer-proxy` must name exactly one socks5 hop; other chains fail at load time (validate_udp_chains). `reality-opts`, `shadow-tls-opts`, `restls-opts` and `jls-opts` require `tls: true` (Mihomo rejects them without TLS), so with TLS off a non-empty block fails; with TLS on, a non-empty block fails as not implemented. Keys the pinned type does not declare at all (`smux`, `ss-opts` on vless, `udp` on http, any unknown name) are ignored exactly as Mihomo ignores them.

proxies.reason: twelve protocol types with their implemented transports, options and UDP associations (ss/trojan); every other type or option is rejected by name

rule-providers.reason: file/http/inline vehicles; yaml/text/mrs; domain/ipcidr/classical; provider paths are lexically confined to the configuration root or SAFE_PATHS (pinned IsSafePath); a classical provider rejects an unsupported/malformed entry by name instead of dropping it; path-in-bundle is named. Explicit update swaps snapshots and keeps the old generation on failure. The declared interval is parsed but not scheduled; hosts/T25 call the update API.

proxy-providers.reason: file/http/inline vehicles; filter/exclude-filter split on a backtick; exclude-type split on |; override (udp, skip-cert-verify, dialer-proxy, additional-prefix/suffix, proxy-name) applied; other pinned override fields, age-secret-key, and group use/providers are named/rejected. An explicit group URL registration creates one `HealthCheck` ticker per provider (deduped by URL, first expected-status kept, filters merged); it also activates a disabled provider and its `check()` probes the provider's own `hc.url` alongside the registered URLs.

tun.reason: disabled block is inert with a warning; enable: true is rejected by name when it reaches the config loader. The device entries never pass it: the host strips it for the Rust engine on every platform and Android hands the VpnService fd as `--tun-fd` (iOS uses the Packet Tunnel's own packetFlow). A desktop Rust session therefore serves only the mixed listener and does not create or take over a TUN device (desktop TUN belongs to T6/Mihomo); status must not read as desktop Rust TUN support.

dns.reason: Implemented for the shapes a pinned v1.19.34 configuration can observe: nameserver/default-nameserver/fallback/fallback-filter/nameserver-policy/proxy-server-nameserver(+policy)/direct-nameserver, respect-rules, ipv6/ipv6-timeout, enhanced-mode normal/redir-host/fake-ip, fake-ip-range(6)/fake-ip-filter(blacklist|whitelist)/fake-ip-ttl, use-hosts/use-system-hosts, cache-algorithm lru|arc (arc served by the LRU cache), cache-max-size, listen (UDP+TCP A/AAAA/CNAME only) and prefer-h3 (recorded; DoH uses HTTP/1.1). `fallback-filter.geoip-code` keeps a leading `!` exactly like the pinned not-matcher plus the fallback filter's inversion. Unimplemented upstream forms are rejected by name: quic:// DoQ, system://, dhcp://, ts/et overlay DNS, rcode://, #h3=true, EDNS client subnet, name-cert-verify, #proxy names and fake-ip-filter-mode rule.

proxy-groups.reason: T23: select/url-test/fallback/load-balance with nested groups, `proxies` (inline/DIRECT/REJECT/REJECT-DROP/COMPATIBLE), `use` providers, include-all/include-all-proxies/include-all-providers (an empty include-all-proxies expansion uses the configured empty-fallback name (REJECT blocks instead of dialing COMPATIBLE, and DIRECT keeps the DIRECT member name; the default is COMPATIBLE)), backtick-separated filter/exclude-filter, `|`-separated exclude-type compared against the pinned adapter name, interval/timeout/lazy/max-failed-times/expected-status/tolerance, default-selected, disable-udp/hidden/icon and empty-fallback. Health checks probe once at startup and again after a provider snapshot swap regardless of lazy; group tasks use the group lastTouch, provider tasks use the provider's own lazy/lastTouch, real dials touch every group on the path (including nested groups) and their use providers. An explicit group URL registers on each `use` provider's single `HealthCheck` (one interval/ticker per provider, extra URLs deduped by URL with merged filters); registration activates a provider whose `health-check.enable` is false and the same check also probes the provider's own `hc.url`. `relay` is rejected with the pinned v1.19.34 removal message. load-balance strategies: consistent-hashing (deterministic FNV-1a key; pinned maphash uses a per-process random seed), round-robin, sticky-sessions. hash-key `in-user` is named as unimplemented. Rule targets may name a group.

profile.reason: `store-selected` is implemented: selections persist to `<cache-dir>/cache.yaml` (pinned stores the same map in bbolt cache.db) and are restored before traffic. A cache directory is host-supplied; without one the kernel warns. `store-fake-ip` is accepted with a warning: fake-ip allocations are in-memory and do not survive a restart (cache.db persistence is a named gap).

hosts.reason: Domain trie with the pinned exact / `*.x` (one label) / `.x` (subdomains) / `+.x` (name and any depth) / `sub.*.x` semantics and the pinned static > `*` > `.` priority; IP lists, domain-valued entries with cycle rejection, the built-in `localhost -> 127.0.0.1`, and `use-system-hosts` for rule-time and DNS-server lookups. On dns.listen an IP entry answers directly and a domain-valued entry replaces the question name, resolves the target and prepends a CNAME (TTL 10), as pinned `withHosts` does in every enhanced mode. `lan` (interface addresses) is rejected by name.

ipv6.reason: General IPv6 switch (pinned default true), combined with dns.ipv6 as pinned (`ipv6 && dns.ipv6`). With IPv6 off, rule-time lookups ask A only and the DNS server answers an empty AAAA; with it on, A and AAAA are joined with the pinned 100ms ipv6-timeout.

external-controller-tls.reason: TLS listener using the pinned top-level tls.certificate/tls.private-key PEMs; ALPN h2/http1.1 advertised, HTTP/1.1 served.

external-controller-cors.reason: allow-origins/allow-private-network; defaults match pinned (['*'], true). Preflight is unauthenticated and always adds Vary: Origin.

secret.reason: Bearer authentication on TCP/TLS plus ?token= for WebSocket upgrades; 401 {"message":"Unauthorized"} before route handlers. Routing precedes auth, like pinned chi.

external-controller-pipe.reason: Windows named pipe is not implemented; rejected by name (use TCP, Unix or TLS).

external-controller-routing-mark.reason: socket routing mark is not applied; rejected by name

socks5.udp: implemented: RFC 1928 `UDP ASSOCIATE`; the control connection stays open and datagrams carry the SOCKS5 address header to the server relay (a `dialer-proxy` chain is rejected for this UDP form because the association dials the server directly); the same association is the packet-tunnel (iOS/Android TUN) UDP transport, so device flows use the SOCKS5 relay rather than a DIRECT fallback
socks5.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).

http.udp: not applicable: Mihomo's HTTP outbound has no UDP option, so any `udp` key is rejected as a non-Mihomo option
http.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).

ss.udp: implemented: AEAD-2017 datagrams (`salt || sealed(addr || payload)`), replies decrypted with the server's salt; `udp-over-tcp: true` switches to sing UoT (v2 magic `sp.v2.udp-over-tcp.arpa`, v1 legacy framing) instead; the pinned outbound opens one UoT stream per destination, so the relay keeps one association per target; with `dialer-proxy` the datagrams travel through exactly one socks5 hop's UDP relay (any other chain fails at load time)
ss.cipherNamedRejections: The pinned ss outbound uses `sing-shadowsocks2` and accepts 39 method names; the other 34 are rejected by name (never silently accepted): legacy AEAD additions (chacha8-ietf-poly1305, xchacha8-ietf-poly1305, rabbit128-poly1305, aes-128/192/256-ccm, aes-128/256-gcm-siv, aegis-128l, aegis-256, aez-384, deoxys-ii-256-128, lea-128/192/256-gcm, ascon128, ascon128a), shadowstream (aes-128/192/256-ctr, aes-128/192/256-cfb, rc4-md5, chacha20-ietf, xchacha20, chacha20), `none`, and 2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm, 2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm, 2022-blake3-chacha20-poly1305, 2022-blake3-chacha8-poly1305, 2022-blake3-aes-128-ccm, 2022-blake3-aes-256-ccm. `DUMMY` is not an ss method in the pinned engine either. The full value matrix and the pinned `-t` verdicts are in evidence/t28-option-parity.{md,json}.
ss.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name). AEAD ciphers follow the pinned ss outbound (`sing-shadowsocks2`) names for aes-128/192/256-gcm, chacha20-ietf-poly1305 and xchacha20-ietf-poly1305 (the 24-byte XChaCha nonce is honoured); every other pinned-accepted name (the shadowstream list, ChaCha8/AES-CCM/GCM-SIV/AEGIS/AEZ/Deoxys/LEA/Ascon AEADs, `none` and the `2022-blake3-*` methods) is a named rejection, enumerated value by value in evidence/t28-option-parity.{md,json}.

trojan.udp: implemented: command 3 over TLS with `addr|length|CRLF|payload` frames; the server connection is established through the `dialer-proxy` chain exactly like TCP (one socks5 hop)
trojan.ssOptsCipherNamedRejections: Pinned `core.PickCipher` accepts 21 method names for `ss-opts.method`: the five implemented AEADs, `chacha8-ietf-poly1305`, `xchacha8-ietf-poly1305`, `aes-128/192/256-ccm`, the ten shadowstream ciphers and the `DUMMY` passthrough. The other 16 are rejected by name: chacha8-ietf-poly1305, xchacha8-ietf-poly1305, aes-128/192/256-ccm, shadowstream (aes-128/192/256-ctr, aes-128/192/256-cfb, rc4-md5, chacha20-ietf, xchacha20, chacha20) and `DUMMY` (case-insensitive). `core.PickCipher` also rejects rabbit128-poly1305, aes-128/256-gcm-siv, aegis-128l, aegis-256, aez-384, deoxys-ii-256-128, lea-128/192/256-gcm, ascon128 and ascon128a (`mihomo -t` reports `cipher not supported` for each), as well as `none` and the six 2022-blake3-* methods; this kernel rejects those too. The full value matrix is in evidence/t28-option-parity.{md,json}.
trojan.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).
trojan.reason: T28 adds `ss-opts` (a bare Shadowsocks AEAD layer over the TLS/WS stream, method/password validated; AES-128-GCM, AES-192-GCM, AES-256-GCM, CHACHA20-IETF-POLY1305 and XCHACHA20-IETF-POLY1305 are implemented). The other 16 names `core.PickCipher` accepts, including `DUMMY`, are rejected by name and enumerated in evidence/t28-option-parity.{md,json}; the 12 legacy AEAD names it no longer accepts are rejected by both engines. The remaining named gaps are the uTLS fingerprint, ECH/REALITY/ShadowTLS/Restls/JLS handshakes and the gRPC transport.

anytls.udp: implemented: `udp: true` opens a UoT stream (`sp.v2.udp-over-tcp.arpa`) and frames `u16 length || payload`; one stream per destination (pinned `ListenPacketContext`), the server connection honours the TCP `dialer-proxy` chain, and the idle-session pool honours the reuse knobs; tested against the pinned anytls listener
anytls.notes: Session reuse follows the pinned `anytls/session.Client`: idle sessions are pooled per outbound, `disable-reuse` closes a session when its stream ends, `min-idle-session`/`idle-session-timeout` bound the sweep, a background ticker runs every `idle-session-check-interval` (started on the first pooled session, aborted with the pool), and intervals/timeouts `<= 5s` are normalised to the pinned 30s. `client-metadata` is sent in the settings frame. A UoT association is opened per destination (the pinned `ListenPacketContext` shape) and its AnyTLS server connection honours the same single-socks5 `dialer-proxy` hop as TCP. `shadow-tls-opts`/`restls-opts`/`jls-opts` remain named rejections: rustls cannot set the uTLS session id / rewrite the ClientHello+ServerHello random those modes need. `client-fingerprint` is applied as the closest rustls profile (browser key-exchange list); extension order/ciphers are not reproduced, so the 4 family rows are approximations counted as residuals, never byte parity. BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).
anytls.security: implemented for jls-opts and shadow-tls-opts versions 1 and 2: the JLS ClientHello/ServerHello random is sealed and verified over a TCP rustls session built from the recorded-random provider (`src/outbound/jls.rs::tcp_client`, `src/outbound/tls_io.rs`), ShadowTLS v1 runs the TLS 1.2 camouflage handshake and then hands the raw stream back (pinned `serverV1` splices raw traffic), and ShadowTLS v2 frames `HMAC-SHA1(read bytes)[..8]` inside the first TLS application-data record with TLS 1.3 session tickets disabled so the pinned server's write hash boundary matches. All three are verified end to end against the pinned anytls listener (`jls-config`/`shadow-tls` inbound blocks). ShadowTLS v3 stays a named rejection: the account lives in the ClientHello session id and the post-handshake records chain HMAC/kdf state, but rustls generates the session id internally (rewriting it invalidates the transcript). Restls stays a named rejection because it rewrites TLS handshake bytes rustls has already authenticated.

gost-relay.reason: TCP relay with optional TLS, username/password authentication, `forward`, the UDP association and the version-1 smux session. The controlled peer is the loopback relay v2 server in tests/protocols.rs, written from transport/gost/relay.go; the smux frame layout is pinned by a unit test. The controlled peer is also driven by the pinned `gost.NewRelayDialer` (`tool/kernel-compat/peers/gost-relay-harness`, with mux and UDP), so the UDP association and the smux session are not only checked against our own client.

mux (smux DefaultConfig version 1, keep-alive disabled, one stream per dial)

ssh.reason: password and inline-PEM public-key authentication, host-key pinning and one direct-tcpip channel per dial; a private-key file path is rejected by name and each dial opens its own SSH client (Mihomo reuses one client per proxy).

The SSH server connection is dialled by the shared outbound dialer (`connect_tcp` then `russh::client::connect_stream`), so these knobs are applied to the real socket instead of a `TcpStream` created inside russh.

ssr.reason: every pinned stream cipher plus every protocol plugin (origin, auth_sha1_v4, auth_aes128_md5, auth_aes128_sha1, auth_chain_a, auth_chain_b), every obfs plugin (plain, http_simple, http_post, random_head, tls1.2_ticket_auth, tls1.2_ticket_fastauth) and the UDP association. The wire format is checked against an independent Go peer built from the pinned packages (`tool/kernel-compat/peers/ssr-plugins`), which also runs the pinned client packages against itself. random_head locates the peer head by scanning the CRC from the longest candidate: the pinned CRC check is not unique for every length (crc32(head[:n-1]) can match the four bytes at n-1), and an ascending scan occasionally took the head one byte short and misaligned the cipher stream.
options: cipher (rc4-md5, aes-128/192/256-cfb, aes-128/192/256-ctr, chacha20, chacha20-ietf, xchacha20, none)
protocol-param (user id and key; the plugin's own parsing)
udp (the pinned cipher.PacketConn + protocol.PacketConn association; no obfs layer, as in the pinned outbound)
ssr.udp: implemented: `udp: true` opens the pinned association (IV || cipher(protocol packet), SOCKS5 address inside, no obfs). Every protocol is verified against the Go peer and a wrong password is rejected. Limit inherited from the pinned client: `auth_aes128_*` datagrams are sealed with the derived user key but opened with the cipher key, so a `protocol-param` breaks the UDP path in both directions; the UDP tests therefore use no protocol-param (TCP with `protocol-param` is covered).
ssr.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).

mieru.reason: TCP single sessions are implemented and the shared stream dialer applies `tfo`/`mptcp`/`interface-name`/`routing-mark`/`ip-version` (T28); the UDP transport, `udp: true` (UDP associate), the multiplexing levels and `traffic-pattern` are rejected at load with the reason recorded (T13 scope)
mieru.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` (the UDP-associate wrapper) is rejected; TCP sessions only
notes: the mieru module is GPL-3.0, so the client is an independent implementation of docs/protocol.md (PBKDF2-SHA256 time salt, XChaCha20-Poly1305 implicit nonce with the user hint, 32-byte metadata, session/data segments, one TCP session per underlay); no mieru code is vendored or linked
handshake-mode values load: HANDSHAKE_NO_WAIT only defers the same handshake, and the kernel dials eagerly
port-range picks a random member per dial (up to four tries) because any port in the range is a valid server endpoint

masque.reason: T18 implements both shapes the pinned adapter serves; T21 adds TCP termination for CONNECT-IP. (1) RFC 9484 CONNECT-IP over HTTP/3 for the Cloudflare WARP configuration: the base64 SEC1 P-256 client key generates the pinned adapter's self-signed client certificate, `public-key` (a DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo) pins the endpoint certificate, and the request is `:method CONNECT`, `:protocol cf-connect-ip`, `:scheme https`, `:authority`/`:path` from `uri` (default https://cloudflareaccess.com) with `capsule-protocol: ?1`. ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT is sent and ADDRESS_ASSIGN/ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT are read; whole IPv4/IPv6 packets travel as HTTP Datagrams. UDP is served by the in-tree UDP codec and TCP by the in-tree minimal TCP client (`outbound/tcp.rs`: active open, SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK, data/ACK, FIN/RST, MSS and peer-window limits, retransmission with RFC 6298-style backoff, fast retransmit, in-order delivery with bounded reordering, half-close); one tunnel and one TCP connection per `dial`. the `ip`, `ipv6`, `mtu`, `ip-stack`, `remote-dns-resolve` and `dns` options keep their T18 semantics. (2) The RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset from T14 still serves a plain server with `udp: true`; it carries UDP only (RFC 9298 has no TCP path), so a TCP dial through that shape is refused by name. `network: h2|h3-l4proxy`, the QUIC `bbr-profile` and meta BBR v1 (quinn has one BBR sender, which is the pinned `bbr`/`bbr_meta_v2` alias, and no v1/profile selector), `dialer-proxy`, gVisor and passive/simultaneous-open TCP are named.
masque.udp: implemented in both shapes. CONNECT-IP: one UDP flow (local source port) per destination, at most 32 flows per association (least-recently-used eviction beyond that), packets built with IPv4 header/UDP checksums or the mandatory IPv6 UDP checksum, `mtu` (pinned default 1280) bounding one datagram, replies matched by (local address, local port, remote address); tunnel DNS is a UDP A/AAAA query to the configured name servers. CONNECT-UDP: one request stream per destination, DATAGRAM capsules with context ID 0, closed flows reclaimed before the cap is enforced.
rejectedAtLoad: congestion-controller: bbr_meta_v1 (quinn has no meta BBR v1 sender)
notImplemented: TCP over CONNECT-UDP (RFC 9298 carries UDP only; TCP needs the CONNECT-IP/WARP shape)
passive TCP (the kernel only initiates), simultaneous open, TCP urgent data
window scaling (RFC 7323), SACK and timestamps are not negotiated
ip-stack.mode: gvisor (the pinned build-tagged gVisor dependency)
congestion-controller: bbr_meta_v1 (quinn has no meta BBR v1 sender)
remote-dns-resolve with DNS over TCP/DoT/DoH or `#param` name servers
ADDRESS_REQUEST from the peer (no address-assignment policy)
IPv6 extension headers and IPv4 fragments (reported and dropped, not reassembled)
DATA frames larger than 2 KiB, capsules larger than 1536 bytes and more than 32 UDP flows per association (local bounds)
TCP retransmission is go-back-N on the oldest unacked segment with a fixed 1 s initial RTO (no RTT estimation), a 64 KiB send/receive buffer and no persist timer on a zero window
notes: the client is written from RFC 9484, 9298, 9297, 9220, 9114 and 793/1122/6298 plus the pinned adapter's recorded configuration shape; no pinned Go code (metacubex/connect-ip-go, mipstack, gVisor, quic-go, metacubex/http) is vendored, linked or copied. DER/base64/calendar helpers, the IP/UDP codec and the TCP state machine are original code; the ECDSA signature comes from `ring`, already the TLS provider

the controlled CONNECT-IP peer in tests/quic_peers.rs is an independent quinn HTTP/3 server with its own IPv4/IPv6 TCP and UDP codecs; it requires the WARP client certificate, advertises 0x08/0x33/0x276, answers `cf-connect-ip`, assigns addresses and echoes tunnelled TCP (SYN-ACK, data, FIN) and UDP
no pinned-binary masque interop is claimed: the pinned adapter has no listener and a WARP registration endpoint is not reachable offline

T7 memory: a UDP association is ~5.14 MB decimal and a TCP dial (one tunnel + one connection) ~5.2 MB decimal analytic worst case, both dominated by T10's 4.7 MB of QUIC windows; see t18-feasibility.json and t21-feasibility.json. The engine opens one tunnel per UDP ASSOCIATE and one per TCP dial, so T7 must cap concurrent masque sessions
`name-cert-verify` is a pinned placeholder that verifies nothing, so it is accepted as a no-op; `skip-cert-verify` drops the endpoint-key pin exactly like the pinned option

the shipped CLI process is covered: cli.rs::process_loads_t18_masque_connect_ip, family_cli.rs::cli_process_tunnels_udp_through_masque_connect_ip and family_cli.rs::cli_process_tunnels_tcp_through_masque_connect_ip

sudoku.reason: TCP sessions with the legacy HTTP mask, the pure and packed downlink codecs, table rotation, all three record AEAD methods, the session mux (`multiplex: on`) and `dialer-proxy` (the exit's server connection is carried by a socks5 hop chain, repaired in T17-A3) are translated from the pinned GPL-3.0 `transport/sudoku` (T17); the HTTP tunnel modes (`stream`/`poll`/`auto`/`ws`) and the UoT association are rejected at load with the reason recorded. T28: the shared stream dialer applies `tfo`/`mptcp`/`interface-name`/`routing-mark`/`ip-version`.
sudoku.license: GPL-3.0-derived translation of Mihomo `transport/sudoku` v1.19.34 (commit 0455d0d28c4526937380505153e65a843d8612e8); the kernel workspace is GPL-3.0-only, any distribution of the combined work must follow GPL-3.0 (source availability etc.), see native-kernel/COPYING.GPL-3.0 and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md
sudoku.udp: not implemented: `udp: true` (the UoT association, `KIPTypeStartUoT` + `transport/sudoku/uot.go`) is rejected at load; the kernel's UDP association selection for sudoku is a T9 decision
notes: the module files carry `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only` and the upstream version/commit; `src/keys.rs` (`sudoku_seed`) and `src/proxies.rs` (`SudokuOutbound`, `parse_sudoku`) are mixed files with the same header on the derived item and the scope stated in their module docs; distribution must follow GPL-3.0 (native-kernel/COPYING.GPL-3.0)

`dialer-proxy`: the dispatch builds the exit's server connection through the hop chain (`src/outbound/mod.rs::connect_via_hops`) and runs the sudoku handshake over it; the exit is never dropped, and exits other than socks5/sudoku (whose protocols cannot run over a stream) fail with a named chain error instead of letting a hop dial the target. The mux session cache key includes the hop chain and is cleared when the engine stops; with `multiplex: on` a new session performs the KIP `StartMux` handshake over the hop tunnel and a cache hit reuses the session without opening a hop connection (T17-A4)

multiplex is the translated client side of `transport/sudoku/multiplex/session.go` (frames open/data/close/reset/ping/pong, one shared session per configuration, recreated after failure); frames are queued whole so streams do not interleave
the HTTP tunnel modes are a mihomo extension (`transport/sudoku/obfs/httpmask/tunnel_*`, ~1.8k lines) and stay rejected by name; the legacy header mask is implemented
tables are built once per configuration (288-grid shuffle, 1820 puzzle candidates per byte) and cached in-process
`multiplex: auto` behaves like `off`: the pinned mode only reuses an HTTP tunnel connection, and the HTTP tunnel layer is rejected
evidence: tests/mihomo_peers.rs (13 sudoku cases: entropy/ascii/directional/custom/rotation tables, packed downlink, three AEAD methods, with/without the HTTP mask, private/public key material, a dialer-proxy chain through a recording SOCKS5 hop, and multiplex: on over that chain; wrong key and mismatched table type)

tuic.reason: TUIC v5 over QUIC: uuid/password authentication (TLS exporter token), one TCP stream per session, request-timeout, congestion-controller (cubic/new_reno/bbr; `cwnd` only inside the BBR branch, as the pinned SetCongestionController does), receive windows and disable-mtu-discovery mapped onto quinn's transport config. The legacy v4 token (BLAKE3 TKN), the UDP relay modes, 0-RTT, the meta BBR profiles (`bbr_meta_v1`/`bbr_meta_v2`) and `bbr-profile` are rejected by name; one QUIC connection is created per dial instead of the pinned pool.
tuic.udp: not implemented: the engine's UDP association has no TUIC datagram/uni-stream relay; UDP traffic routed to TUIC is dropped and logged
notImplemented: congestion-controller: bbr_meta_v1 (quinn has no meta BBR v1 sender)
tuic.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).

hysteria.reason: Hysteria v1 over QUIC: TCP with the binary control hello (auth/auth-str, up/down) and one stream per session; recv-window-conn/recv-window and disable-mtu-discovery are applied to quinn's transport config. Port hopping, the XPlus obfuscator, the faketcp/wechat transports, UDP datagrams and 0-RTT are rejected by name.
hysteria.udp: not implemented: the engine has no Hysteria UDP session relay; `udp` traffic routed to Hysteria is dropped and logged
hysteria.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).

hysteria2.reason: Hysteria2 over QUIC: HTTP/3 authentication (`/auth`, status 233), one TCP stream per session with the 0x401 request frame, BBR with `cwnd` as the initial window (pinned default 32 packets), the initial/max stream/connection receive windows mapped to quinn, `up` as a Brutal sender (pinned window formula), `bbr-profile` mapped to the BBR initial window (quinn has no profile selector; the profile now takes precedence over `cwnd`), `udp-mtu` mapped to the QUIC initial path MTU, Salamander and Gecko obfuscation, `ports`/`hop-interval` port hopping on a wrapped `quinn::AsyncUdpSocket`, and the realm rendezvous client (HTTP control `/connect`, STUN discovery, HYRLMv1 hole punching, then QUIC over the punched socket). The realm control TLS block keeps its `fingerprint` (SHA-256 certificate DER pin, enforced even with `skip-cert-verify`) and presents `certificate`/`private-key` as the control mTLS identity; both are validated at load, and `realm-opts` with a non-empty `ports` pool is the pinned `realm and port hopping are mutually exclusive` error. UDP is implemented as the pinned QUIC datagram session (`udp.rs::Hysteria2Udp`: session/packet/fragment header, `host:port` address field, fragmentation at `udp-mtu`, packet-id reassembly with the pinned 10 s age on incomplete messages) and is relayed on both the mixed SOCKS5 and TUN paths; the pinned outbound enables UDP unconditionally, so `udp: true|false` is a tolerated no-op. A `dialer-proxy` chain is accepted at load (the pinned client accepts it) and refused by name only by the association at dial time, because a QUIC socket cannot ride a SOCKS5 UDP hop; the whole configuration is never rejected. `ech-opts` stays rejected by name, unchanged from T30.
options: client-fingerprint (approximation: closest rustls profile, counted as residual)
hysteria2.udp: implemented: QUIC datagram session (`session id | packet id | fragment id/count | varint address | host:port | data`), one session per association, any destination per message, `udp-mtu` fragmentation with packet-id reassembly and a 10 s age on incomplete messages; relayed by the mixed SOCKS5 and TUN paths
hysteria2.notes: BasicOption dialer knobs are applied by the shared stream dialer: tfo (Linux TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT, macOS TCP_FASTOPEN), mptcp (IPPROTO_MPTCP, TCP fallback when the stack lacks it), interface-name (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux, IP_BOUND_IF/IPV6_BOUND_IF on macOS), routing-mark (SO_MARK on Linux; accepted and logged on other platforms exactly like the pinned dialer) and ip-version (address-family filter/order for the proxy-server name).

shadowquic.reason: TCP and UDP (QUIC datagrams and `udp-over-stream`) are implemented against the pinned listener with an independent JLS random seal and a protocol-level transport; provenance is in tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t15-cleanroom.md; `zero-rtt`, QUIC `v2` and the private Brutal congestion options are rejected by name because quinn has no Brutal controller/JLS 0-RTT ticket. T28: the QUIC endpoint applies `interface-name`/`routing-mark`/`ip-version`; `tfo`/`mptcp` are accepted no-ops because the pinned packet dialer cannot apply TCP options to a QUIC UDP socket.
shadowquic.notes: recv-window defaults follow the kernel T7 budget (512 KiB stream / 2 MiB connection) rather than the pinned 1.57 MiB / 6.4 MiB initial windows; those are local flow-control choices, not wire fields. max-datagram-frame-size sizes the datagram buffers; the usable datagram payload is also path-MTU-bound, so larger UDP packets use udp-over-stream.

wireguard.reason: The WireGuard transport (Noise IK, cookie reply, pre-shared key, transport keys, padding, replay window, initiator rekey, keepalive) is implemented in src/outbound/wireguard.rs and verified against the locked metacubex/wireguard-go device; TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the userspace IP stack and TUN device owned by T6/T7, so dial() refuses with that gap named. AmneziaWG, an explicit ip-stack mode, the stack resolver and endpoint refresh are rejected by name.
wireguard.notes: Both peer forms load: `peers:` and the embedded top-level server/port/public-key form. `allowed-ips` defaults to 0.0.0.0/0 and/or ::/0 from ip/ipv6 in the single-peer form; `mtu` defaults to 1408. The transport is initiator-only for rekeys (it rekeys before the responder's 120 s window); answering a server-initiated handshake is not implemented.
wireguard.license: No wireguard/boringtun crate; no Go source vendored, linked, or translated. The locked MIT wireguard-go device is a test peer only. The pinned adapter/outbound/wireguard.go (GPL-3.0) was read for option names/defaults; this is source consultation, not a certified clean-room. Audit and limits: tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t16-provenance.md.

tailscale.reason: The control-base Noise IK transport, the HTTP/2 /machine/map request and the DERP greeting/client-info/ping/packet frames are implemented in src/outbound/tailscale.rs and verified against a controlled peer built from the locked BSD-3-Clause tailscale module. Node registration is not implemented, so hostname/auth-key/state-dir/ephemeral/accept-routes:true/exit-node/exit-node-allow-lan-access:true are rejected at load. TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack and TUN device, so dial() refuses with that gap named.
tailscale.notes: control-url is used by the protocol layer; the control server key is a library parameter. Registration-only options are explicit rejections, not silently accepted. Basic socket-shaping options and dialer-proxy are rejected with the T6/T7 boundary.
tailscale.license: No Tailscale source is copied or linked; the locked BSD-3-Clause module is a test peer only. See tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t19-mesh.md.

zerotier.reason: Identity generation/parsing (address proof of work), planet/moon parsing, VL1 packet armor (Salsa20/12 + Poly1305 and protocol-13 extended HELLO), HELLO/OK/WHOIS/ECHO and the VL2 frame payload are implemented in src/outbound/zerotier.rs and verified against a controlled peer built from the locked MPL-2.0 zerotier-go module. An explicit ip-stack, remote-dns-resolve/dns, remote trace and the TCP fallback transport (force/non-empty relay) are rejected with the T6/T7/T5 boundary. TCP/UDP through the network needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack, and the controller membership exchange is T5, so dial() refuses with that gap named.
zerotier.notes: tcp-fallback-mode auto/disable with an empty relay is accepted because it asks for no transport; force or a non-empty relay is rejected. The controller membership/config verbs are T5.
zerotier.license: No ZeroTier source is copied or linked; the locked MPL-2.0 module is a test peer only. See tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t19-mesh.md.

easytier.reason: T20 translated the locked EasyTier LGPL-3.0-or-later source: the real DefaultHasher network_secret_digest, 16-byte little-endian PeerManagerHeader/TCP frame, HandshakeRequest/PingPong, Noise XX handshake (msg1/2/3, secret proof, root key) and the secure-datagram AES-GCM/ChaCha20 data path are implemented in src/outbound/easytier.rs and verified against the pinned wasm core with enable_encryption=false and with SecureMode()+Encryption(true). TCP/UDP through the tunnel and OSPF/route host identity need T6/T7; hostname/ipv4/dhcp and the remaining options are rejected by name.
easytier.notes: Secure-datagram/Noise XX is now implemented and verified; OSPF/route host identity (hostname/ipv4/dhcp), KCP/QUIC, private-mode, exit-node/DNS, mapped-listeners and proxied networks are rejected by name. `enable-encryption: true` is accepted only with `secure-mode: true` (the source encrypts only through the Noise/secure-datagram session); the pair is implemented, `enable-encryption` alone is rejected by name. Device/TUN is T6/T7. Public translation revision 45a6b6f1769f95590a396f4962e58d654b6e0380; pinned wasm reports 5f1eaa7c9f9d3e89e9b75a6d87531a436fae40c4 (not public).

openvpn.reason: The control channel (UDP/TCP framing, hard reset, reliable ACKs, TLS 1.2/1.3 client authentication, key-method 2) and the AEAD data channel are implemented in src/outbound/openvpn.rs and verified against OpenVPN 2.7.9; TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack and TUN device, so dial() refuses with that gap named. tls-auth/tls-crypt, compression and CBC data ciphers are rejected by name.
openvpn.notes: `ca` is an inline PEM and is required; the server chain is verified against it without a hostname check (matching the pinned client). `cert`/`key` are inline PEM and optional; without them the server may reject the TLS client (observed as a bounded handshake timeout). The data ciphers are AES-128-GCM, AES-256-GCM and CHACHA20-POLY1305; AES-192-GCM and CBC are not implemented.
openvpn.license: No OpenVPN crate; no OpenVPN/Mihomo source vendored, linked, or copied line-by-line. The GPL-2.0 OpenVPN binary is a test peer only. The pinned transport/openvpn (GPL-3.0) was read for functional wire facts; this is not a certified clean-room. Audit and limits: tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t16-provenance.md.

mixed.reason: one mixed port (HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS5 CONNECT + SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE) from `mixed-port`/`socks-port`; the top-level `listeners:` section is rejected until T5
notImplemented: UDP over the mixed port's HTTP side

socks.reason: SOCKS5 CONNECT and UDP ASSOCIATE are served on the mixed port; `listeners: type: socks` is rejected (T5)

http.reason: HTTP CONNECT (and 405 for other methods) on the mixed port; `listeners: type: http` is rejected (T5)

select.reason: first member unless `default-selected`/API/cache fixes one; `fixed` selection survives provider updates; `disable-udp` drops UDP datagrams (pinned SupportUDP).

url-test.reason: pinned fast()-algorithm: first member until probes exist, then lowest LastDelayForTestUrl among alive members, `tolerance` keeps the current node (on a later resolution; the pinned `fastNotExist` first-member quirk is reproduced), fixed selection wins while alive, on-dial-failure thresholds trigger a health check. The startup check runs immediately even with the default lazy/interval config, and probes dial through the member's full dialer-proxy chain. A `now`/dial resolution reuses the previous computation for ten seconds (pinned `URLTest.fastSingle`); `select` (pinned `ForceSet`, which resets only `fastSingle`) and a dial-failure-triggered check reset it, the periodic probe does not. `fastNode` survives `ForceSet`, so the tolerance baseline still applies when the fixed selection is unavailable.

fallback.reason: first member AliveForTestUrl; a fixed selection that died is cleared and scanning continues; members with no probe record yet are alive (pinned initial alive=true).

load-balance.reason: consistent-hashing/round-robin/sticky-sessions implemented with pinned jumpHash; retry on dead members and full traversal fallback. The consistent-hashing bucket mapping is not byte-identical to pinned because pinned hashes with a per-process random maphash seed; `hash-key: in-user` is rejected by name.

relay.reason: pinned v1.19.34 removed the relay type (`unsupported type: The group [x] with relay type was removed, please using dialer-proxy instead`); the Rust kernel reproduces that named rejection instead of implementing a type the pinned engine refuses.

PROCESS-PATH.reason: process metadata is matched when the host supplies it; the mixed inbound has no process lookup

PROCESS-NAME-REGEX.reason: regex form implemented with the Rust regex crate (look-around/backreferences rejected at load); process lookup is host-supplied

PROCESS-PATH-REGEX.reason: regex form implemented with the Rust regex crate (look-around/backreferences rejected at load); process lookup is host-supplied

DSCP.reason: DSCP metadata is not set by the mixed inbound; rejected by name

IN-USER.reason: per-user inbound metadata is not exposed; rejected by name

IN-NAME.reason: named listeners are T6/T25; rejected by name

REMATCH-NAME.reason: rematch rules are not implemented; rejected by name

PROCESS-NAME-WILDCARD.reason: pinned component/wildcard semantics, case-insensitive, over host-supplied process metadata

PROCESS-PATH-WILDCARD.reason: pinned component/wildcard semantics, case-insensitive, over host-supplied process metadata

familiesNotImplemented.note: T4 delivered 9 outbound types; T11 added gost-relay/ssh/ssr; T10 added tuic/hysteria/hysteria2 (QUIC); T14 added masque (CONNECT-UDP); T15 added shadowquic; T16 added the wireguard/openvpn transport adapters; T17/T18 added sudoku/masque-CONNECT-IP; T19 added tailscale/zerotier (partial; device/TUN remains T6/T7); T20 added the LGPL-3.0-or-later EasyTier cleartext + Noise XX/secure-datagram translation; OSPF/route and device/TUN remain out of scope. T5 owns the built-in direct/dns/reject/rematch adapters.

direct.reason: built-in; DIRECT is already a rule action

dns.reason: built-in adapter that needs the DNS resolver

reject.reason: built-in; REJECT is already a rule action

unmappedNotes: DNS/hosts (T22) resolve names for GEOIP/IP-ASN/IP-CIDR/IP-SUFFIX/RULE-SET IP rules lazily in rule order and honor `no-resolve`; DIRECT and proxy-server names use direct-nameserver/proxy-server-nameserver when `dns.enable` is true. With DNS disabled the OS resolver is the pinned `SystemResolver` equivalent.
Every proxy type outside the implemented ones is rejected at load time with its type named, never ignored; familiesNotImplemented records the task that implements it.
geodata-mode false uses Country.mmdb; geodata-mode true uses GeoIP.dat; GEOSITE always uses GeoSite.dat. MRS rule-provider decoding shares the Tauri mrs.rs algorithm (ported, not shared code).
Proxy-provider health-check fields are parsed and exposed but latency probing is T23; provider updates are exposed through Kernel::update_*_provider for T25.

Proxy groups (T23) are implemented per pinned outboundgroup semantics; rule targets may name them. `dialer-proxy` still resolves only inline proxy names (a group or provider proxy target is a named load rejection), and PASS/PASS-RULE markers remain rejected.

`profile.store-selected` persists fixed group selections; the file is `<cache-dir>/cache.yaml` and hosts must provide a cache directory (the CLI uses the configuration directory). Pinned writes bbolt cache.db, so the file is not interchangeable; the selected-map semantics are.

DoQ, DHCP/system/overlay/rcode nameservers, nameserver #proxy names, EDNS client subnet, name-cert-verify, HTTP/2/3 DoH, fake-ip-filter rule mode, profile.store-fake-ip persistence and non-A/AAAA/CNAME DNS server qtypes are rejected by name (see the dns section).

ignoredByPinnedVersion.note: Keys the pinned type does not declare (or declares only as a no-op in the given configuration) are accepted and ignored, exactly as Mihomo ignores them. They are not compatibility gaps.

ss: client-fingerprint (only read by a plugin, which is rejected)

global: any key no proxy type declares (a typo or a newer option)

quicProfile.tls: rustls 0.23, TLS 1.3 only, ALPN per family (h3 for TUIC/Hysteria2/masque/shadowquic, hysteria for Hysteria v1); shadowquic seals the ClientHello/ServerHello random with JLS and verifies the server random before certificate verification
quicProfile.offlineSource: local cargo registry cache; no h3/qpack/connect-ip/IP-stack/wireguard/mesh/OpenVPN crate is cached. JLS has no Rust crate: T15 implements the random seal in-tree and uses the locked jls-tls package only as a vector generator (tool/kernel-compat/peers/shadowquic-jls-vectors). quinn-proto and typenum became direct dependencies for the session wrapper and the 32-byte GCM nonce; both were already in the lockfile.
quicProfile.memory: one Endpoint + one Connection per dial (masque: per UDP association); transport windows capped to stream receive 512 KiB, connection receive 2 MiB, send 2 MiB, datagram buffers 64 KiB (quinn defaults: 1.25 MB / VarInt::MAX / 10 MB / ~1 MB). masque adds at most 32 request streams per association, each with a 2 x 65,535 B outbound queue and at most 131,102 B of pending capsule data; its per-association worst case (~19 MB decimal, including the QUIC windows) is recorded in t14-feasibility.json. shadowquic uses the same endpoint/connection profile plus one control stream and a 32-packet receive queue per UDP association; its `max-datagram-frame-size` (default 1400) sizes the datagram buffers. T7 must measure the whole iOS extension against the 40,000,000-byte budget; these tasks record the dependency and the caps, not a device measurement.
quicProfile.platform: macOS arm64 loopback and pinned-Mihomo runs; Linux/Android/iOS compile from the same code path; Windows compiles but no run is recorded

groupPolicy: Member expansion follows outboundgroup.GroupBase.GetProxies: inline `proxies` block first, then `use` provider snapshots; filter pieces split on backticks and matched case-sensitively like regexp2.None; multiple providers/filters reorder the combined list by filter; exclude-filter then exclude-type are applied; an empty list becomes `empty-fallback` (default COMPATIBLE). Health state is per (member source, name, test URL): a URL with no record yet is alive and LastDelayForTestUrl is 65535, matching the pinned adapter's initial state. Interval checks run on each task's own interval boundary (select has no automatic check; other types default to 300 s; `lazy: true` skips an interval when the group was not touched recently). A real dial touches every group on the resolved path and its `use` providers; a probe of a nested group also touches it (pinned `Proxy.URLTest` -> `DialContext` -> `GetProxies(true)`), so nested lazy ticks keep probing, while `now`/status reads never touch. Provider `health-check` drives provider members; an explicit group URL registers an extra probe on its `use` providers with the provider's `health-check.timeout` (not the group's), and is ignored when equal to the provider's `health-check.url`. `filter` on a group only filters named providers (the inline/compatible block is never filtered), as in pinned GetProxies.

transports.udp: implemented (default port 53; a TC=1 reply is retried over TCP, like the pinned client)
transports.dot: implemented (default port 853; SNI is the nameserver host, platform+custom roots, `skip-cert-verify`)
transports.doh: implemented over HTTP/1.1 GET `?dns=<base64url>` with Accept: application/dns-message (default 443/80); HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are not used, so prefer-h3 is recorded and #h3=true is rejected
transports.doq: not implemented: quic:// is rejected by name
transports.others: system://, dhcp://, ts://, et://, rcode:// are rejected by name

resolverSemantics.batch: all servers of a list race and the first successful message wins; SERVFAIL/REFUSED answers count as failures (pinned batchExchange)
resolverSemantics.fallback: nameserver-policy wins first; a matching fallback-filter.domain or fallback-filter.geosite sends only the fallback; otherwise main and fallback race and a main answer whose IP is LAN is never replaced, while an IP in fallback-filter.ipcidr or failing the fallback-filter.geoip matcher falls back. fallback-filter.geoip-code keeps a leading `!`: the pinned LoadGeoIPMatcher builds a not-matcher and dnsFallbackFilter inverts it, so `!CN` falls back for a CN answer and `CN` for a non-CN answer
resolverSemantics.cache: question-keyed cache with the minimal TTL over answer+authority records (negative NXDOMAIN/NODATA answers cache through their SOA), SERVFAIL cached for 5s, `cache-max-size` entries; `arc` is accepted but served by the LRU
resolverSemantics.policies: plain-domain keys use the pinned trie (specificity within a contiguous group), `geosite:` and `rule-set:` (domain behavior) use their domain sets in declaration order
resolverSemantics.respectRules: TCP/TLS/HTTPS upstreams follow the rule set and proxy groups (T23); UDP upstreams are rejected by name because proxy UDP routing is not implemented
resolverSemantics.defaultNameserver: used only to bootstrap a nameserver's hostname and validated as pure IPs, like the pinned parse

fakeIp.pool: gateway = network+1, first allocation = network+4, wrap at the broadcast address, reused slots evicted (pinned component/fakeip); the in-memory host store is bounded at 1000 entries (arbitrary eviction under pressure vs the pinned LRU)
fakeIp.filter: blacklist/whitelist domain patterns, plus the hostnames of fallback nameservers (pinned parseDNS)
fakeIp.ttl: fake-ip-ttl (clamped to >=1) on A/AAAA answers; the IP->host mapping and fake pool are in-memory
fakeIp.rebuild: an inbound destination that is a fake IP is mapped back to its host before rules, then resolved through direct/proxy resolvers; an unknown fake IP fails with `fake DNS record <ip> missing`
fakeIp.persistence: profile.store-fake-ip is accepted with a warning: the pool and mapping are in-memory, so allocations do not survive a restart (the pinned cache.db store is a named gap)

server.listen: UDP and TCP on dns.listen; middleware order hosts -> fake-ip -> mapping -> resolver in every enhanced mode. A hosts IP entry answers directly (TTL 10 and a 10s mapping) and a domain-valued entry replaces Question[0].Name with the target, resolves it through the remaining middleware and prepends a CNAME (TTL 10), like pinned withHosts
server.qtypes: A/AAAA/CNAME are answered; other qtypes get NOTIMP (the pinned server forwards every type)

engineIntegration.ruleResolution: GEOIP/IP-ASN/IP-CIDR/IP-SUFFIX/RULE-SET IP rules resolve lazily in first-match order; a failing resolution is remembered and later IP rules do not re-query; `no-resolve` blocks the query (a hosts entry still pre-fills the address, as pinned does)
engineIntegration.direct: DIRECT dials resolve a domain through direct-nameserver (or the main list) when DNS is on, the OS resolver otherwise
engineIntegration.proxyServer: proxy server names resolve through proxy-server-nameserver(+policy) when configured, otherwise the main list
engineIntegration.hosts: configured hosts are applied to a domain destination before the first rule (pinned `resolveMetadata` sets DstIP from DefaultHosts), so an IP rule matches through hosts even with `no-resolve`; hosts are also consulted by rule-time lookups, DIRECT dials and the DNS server even when dns.enable is false
engineIntegration.udp: SOCKS5 UDP destinations follow the same pre-handle/rule/resolve path before a DIRECT send; proxy datagrams keep the domain

notImplemented: system://, dhcp://, ts://, et://, rcode:// nameservers
h3=true / DoH over HTTP/2 or HTTP/3
DNS server forwarding of qtypes other than A/AAAA/CNAME
ARPA/PTR and other non-IP lookup shapes

listeners: external-controller (TCP; a hostless ':PORT' binds [::]:PORT with an IPv4 wildcard fallback; a busy port logs and skips that listener without failing kernel start)
external-controller-tls (HTTP/1.1 only; ALPN advertises http/1.1, unlike pinned which also serves h2)

/configs.reason: GET/PATCH/PUT; PUT builds a replacement generation before swapping and keeps the old one on failure. Changed mixed-port/bind-address/dns.listen/controller listeners are named 400s (restart required).

/proxies.reason: list/detail/select/clear/delay; provider nodes are only under /providers/proxies like pinned

/rules.reason: index/type/payload/proxy/size match; pinned `extra` hit counters are not tracked and omitted

/connections.reason: live TCP tunnels with pinned metadata/byte/chain/rule fields; DELETE closes one or all; UDP associations are closed with the kernel/connection control stream but are not listed individually

/providers/proxies.reason: real providers plus Compatible group/default entries; update failure keeps the old snapshot; Compatible providers resolve member nodes and healthchecks through the group member list / all adapters

/providers/rules.reason: list/update; inline providers report format "" and payload like pinned

/logs.reason: NDJSON/WebSocket stream carries controller events plus host-forwarded tracing events (the CLI forwards all tracing); library hosts must wire KernelOptions::log_bus to their logger; `level` is validated against the pinned keys before the stream starts (400 Body invalid otherwise)

/traffic.reason: one-second up/down deltas from live byte counters

/memory.reason: inuse is the process peak RSS from getrusage; oslimit 0

/configs/geo.reason: geodata download is not started; explicit 404 lets Billow report the missing capability

/group.reason: explicit 404; group data is available under /proxies

/dns/query.reason: explicit 404; DNS resolution exists internally (T22) but the query endpoint is not exposed

/restart.reason: process restart belongs to the host (T6)

websocket /connections/logs/traffic.reason: minimal RFC 6455 text-frame server; client frames are not parsed

knownDivergences: PUT /configs moving mixed-port/bind-address/dns.listen or the controller listener/secret: pinned recreates them; the Rust kernel answers 400 and requires a restart.
PATCH /configs {"tun":{"enable":true}}: pinned answers 204 and attempts a TUN device; the Rust kernel rejects it by name (no device layer before T6/T7).

GET /configs reports only fields this kernel honours; pinned General keys with no equivalent (unified-delay, routing-mark, geox-url, sniffing, find-process-mode, tcp-concurrent, keep-alive) are omitted rather than fabricated.
The /proxies map omits pinned's GLOBAL/PASS/COMPATIBLE builtins; the kernel's routing has no such adapters.
Rule hit statistics (`extra` in /rules) are not tracked.
external-controller-tls advertises http/1.1 only and serves HTTP/1.1 only; pinned also offers h2 and serves it through Go's http server.
A control listener that cannot bind is logged and skipped without failing kernel start (pinned behaviour); the mixed inbound and the other control listeners keep running.
PUT /providers/{proxies,rules}/:name and PUT /configs perform blocking provider I/O on spawn_blocking workers, so the control runtime keeps serving while a provider stalls.
